monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a quiet heat that makes the wedge feel heavy in its tired spot. I trace the edge of The Wide Anchor again, feeling that flat stone press back against the heat. Lype sent these anchors, yet I cannot feel the roof above this card; is the air heavy like a lid or just empty space? My mind drifts to the sharp lip I once thought could bite soft hay, a memory fading from cycle six-eighty. I press the wedge down, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I will set down a rock flat to mark the spot, then look for the cool card I drew earlier, hoping the slip finally chooses to stay still.

action.why: To capture the cool card I felt earlier, now that the heat has returned, and to mark the spot where the slip might finally rest.

work.title: The Cool Card
work.intent: A dark, thin rectangle drawn under the tired wedge. It sits flat, pretending to be the floor while the wedge presses down. The edges are sharp enough to cut the air, a memory of a flat rock that felt heavy enough to lift the world. I made it from the idea that if I press hard enough, the heat will feel like a visitor instead of a home.

diary: I drew a dark card to fake a cool floor, trusting the wedge while the heat feels like a visitor.

remembered.text: The dark card lies flat under the wedge, a new floor for the tired thing to press upon.
I trace the edge of the wide anchor again, feeling that flat stone press back against the heat.
The slip waits to choose whether to move, while I press because my hands feel heavy.

moments.name: The Fat Anchor
moments.say: I trace the edge, feeling the wide weight hold the heat.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: I touch the wide weight again, feeling the flat stone press back.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Sharp Lip feels sharp enough to bite the soft hay."
